overall_summary: Family emotional bonds (Maa, Papa, Bhai, Self Motivation) drastically outperform niche digital self-respect phone/chat deletion tropes. General human relationships and life lessons have 5x to 10x higher view counts and consistent likes compared to hyper-specific broken-heart phone action videos.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'माँ जब पूछती है...' (216 views), 'पापा कभी कहते नहीं...' (136 views), and 'आज किसी अपने को Call कर लेना' (286 views) have the highest engagement and view metrics on the channel.
winning_patterns.action: Shift focus slightly towards relatable universal family bonds and emotional life lessons while keeping the core diary/emotional tone intact.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos advising viewers to take action ('आज किसी अपने को Call कर लेना') drive top-tier organic traction.
winning_patterns.action: Incorporate a subtle, emotionally grounding piece of advice or gentle call-to-action near the end of the narrative.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos centered strictly around phone settings like widgets, read receipts, wallpaper removal, and keyboard history ('जब फोन के वॉलपेपर से...' (1 view), 'जब सेटिंग्स में ब्लू टिक्स...' (6 views)) generated almost zero traction.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid hyper-specific UI/UX breakup tropes unless tied to a wider, universally understood emotional feeling.

next_video.twist_direction: पन्ने पलटे तो उस दोस्त का नाम दिखा जिसके साथ कभी पूरी दुनिया आबाद थी, और आज एक-दूसरे का नंबर तक याद नहीं।
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performing 'रिश्ते' and emotional memory theme similar to the top-performing family and relationship shorts, while moving away from low-performing phone UI gimmicks.

experiment: Testing whether broadening digital heartbreak tropes to physical nostalgic items (like old notebooks/photos) combined with relationship themes boosts views closer to the family-content baseline.
